div.h1: RunPod deployment: the model, the money, and the failure modes
div.p: Two ideas drive almost every mistake below. (1) desiredStatus: RUNNING is a WISH, not an observation — it is what we asked for, not what happened. Billing follows the wish; the container may never start. (2) Only the network volume survives a stop. Everything else is a consequence of those two.

g.text: 2 — Lifecycle, and exactly where money starts
4 — Two ways in, and they fail differently
6 — Every failure we actually hit, and its fix

div.h2: Three nested things, each with its own failure mode

tr.td: having no capacity for the GPU
never starting on that GPU family

div.p: We only ever control the ends. The MACHINE is assigned, which is why pod_up.sh polls myself.pods.machine.maintenance* before resuming: a pod started into a maintenance window bills while its volume is unreachable.
Billing begins at RUNNING. Usability begins three states later. Nothing in the API forces the middle to ever complete, and runpodctl pod list reports RUNNING the whole time.
On 2026-08-07 two H100 pods sat in that gap for 13 and 22 minutes and never left it — runtime: null, ports: [], and the SSH proxy answering container not found. They billed the entire time.
The only honest readiness test is a command that runs ON the pod. desiredStatus cannot distinguish "booting" from "never going to boot".
Holds the synced repo (/root/debate), logs, run outputs.
WIPED on stop. Destroyed on remove. Sized by --containerDiskSize (we use 200 GB).
$VOL in every script. Holds envs/verl-sm90, hf/ (121 GB of weights), uv/cache, wheels/.

Survives stop AND remove. Bills ~$0.07/GB/month while idle. Attached at create with --networkVolumeId; cannot be added later, and it is DATACENTER-LOCAL — only six datacenters offer both volumes and H200.

Reachable without any pod, over S3: https://s3api-<dc-lowercased>.runpod.io, bucket = volume id, using S3 credentials from the console (not the API key). Seed it, migrate it between regions, or pull checkpoints off it from a laptop. Renting a GPU to run rsync is paying a GPU rate to move bytes.

Every run so far has had no network volume, so /workspace was just container disk. That single fact explains the ~80 min of cold provisioning on every pod, and why every stop had to be a remove preceded by a manual evacuation — an evacuation the S3 endpoint would have made unnecessary.
--ports '22/tcp' -> runtime.ports[] gives ip:publicPort.

Fast, supports rsync/scp. Requires runtime to exist, so it is useless in exactly the failure above. scp also silently fails host-key verification where rsync -e ssh with the right flags succeeds — checksum every transfer, never trust exit codes.
<podId>-<hash>@ssh.runpod.io, needs --startSSH and a PTY (ssh -tt).
Works without any port mapping, which makes it the diagnostic channel: it distinguishes "no route" from container not found. That is how the 2026-08-07 pods were finally diagnosed.
pod_up.sh — RESUME only, no create path. Gates on maintenance windows (only visible on the authenticated GraphQL API; the public status page omits them). Exit 8 is the one that means money.

provision_sm90.sh — builds $VOL/envs/verl-sm90. Joint vllm+verl resolve (~25 min), three source patches, flash-attn (~45 min from source, ~1s with FLASH_ATTN_WHEEL=), sanity import gate. Every step bounded by timeout(1).

pod_run.sh — launch lock, trainer guard, judge vLLM (debate mode), then execs the trainer and starts the idle watchdog. Model load + CUDA graph capture takes ~8 min before the first step line — a trainer is not dead because its process is briefly absent.
pod_idle_stop.sh — STOPS, never removes. Evacuates /root to /workspace first, because stop wipes the container disk. Destroying a pod stays a human decision.

tr.td: no --dataCenterId; RunPod picked a region with no stock. H200 was available in 7 DCs the whole time
query runpodctl datacenter list first, create into a named DC
readiness gate: poll for runtime.ports and a successful remote command; auto-delete on deadline
datacenter list / gpu list are the read-only probes
attach one at create — it cannot be added later
about to rebuild an env that already exists elsewhere
assumed a volume needs a pod to touch
it does not: S3 endpoint, no GPU, no hourly rate
truncated wheel transfer; silent scp failure
watcher declared a live run dead
require a step line or 2 consecutive misses past an 8 min grace
idle pod billing after a run

div.h2: Three scripts, each closing one failure above
div.p: pod_create.sh — creation with a bounded downside. Probe datacenter list (read-only) -> refuse unknown (gpu, image) pairs -> create into a NAMED datacenter with the volume attached -> readiness gate: poll until a port exists AND ssh pod true succeeds, deadline ~6 min, then delete the pod. That last step is the point: it turns an open-ended bill into a bounded one. Applied to 2026-08-07 it costs $2 instead of $9. A volume is datacenter-local, so its DC overrides the probe.

pod_sync.sh — transfer, then prove it. rsync, then sha256 both ends and diff PER FILE. Copy exit status is not evidence: scp returned success having moved nothing, and a wheel arrived truncated at 57,446,400 of 62,109,228 bytes. Per-file because GNU sha256sum and BSD shasum disagree on path prefixes and sort order, so an aggregate hash false-alarms even when every file matches.

pod_watch.sh — a verdict only when one is earned. Two consecutive misses AND past a 12-minute grace before believing a death; completion requires the step COUNT to reach target. Absence is not success. Model load plus graph capture runs ~8 min before the first step line, which is how a healthy run got declared dead at 60 seconds.
The volume exists — s3hz0k8153, 1250 GB, AP-IN-2. It pins us to a datacenter that stocks H100 but no H200. Using it means H100; using H200 means re-provisioning from scratch on every pod.

Why the -cluster image never started a container on H100 is unknown. Both dead pods were created with NO --dataCenterId, so they landed wherever RunPod chose — the failure may have been a bad host rather than the GPU family. pod_create.sh refuses the pair rather than explaining it; settling it costs one bounded ~$2 attempt.
